title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has released its response to the Committee's 2020 report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining plans to strengthen accountability, transparency and safety in the use of AI. It sets out new policies and frameworks that aim to protect citizens’ rights while encouraging responsible AI development.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: This policy explains the EU’s new regulation on artificial intelligence, setting unified rules for AI systems across the Union. It also updates other related EU laws to keep them consistent with the new AI rules.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting out how it will regulate the use of artificial intelligence in qualifications, aiming to keep exams fair, transparent and reliable. The policy responds to requests from government officials and outlines measures to prevent cheating, protect data, and ensure AI tools support rather than undermine assessment quality.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how copyrighted works are used to train and develop AI systems and evaluates the legal, economic, and ethical implications of that practice. It offers recommendations for balancing the protection of copyright holders with the need for continued AI innovation and access to creative content.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK Government has released its response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report titled “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency.” The response outlines the government’s plans to strengthen AI regulation, promote innovation, and ensure public safety and trust.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the scope and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence should align with public standards. It also includes FAQs that explain the committee’s purpose, membership, and expected outcomes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee on the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission outlines CSPL’s viewpoints and recommendations for how AI should be regulated and managed.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy looks at how AI changes the rules for medical products and explains how to put the AI White Paper principles into practice. It focuses on keeping AI‑driven medical devices safe, clear, and accountable for manufacturers, regulators, and patients.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organization the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI user among similarly sized defence forces. It outlines a vision for leveraging AI to strengthen strategic capabilities and operational excellence.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport AI Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will work with the transport industry to take advantage of AI technologies while keeping potential risks under control. It outlines strategies for implementing AI, monitoring its impact, and ensuring safety, fairness, and transparency across the sector.
